Comment: "Thus, we can say that the language, which morphologically shows its ergativity only in the third person singular through the actancial indices [verbal person markers], is syntactically fully ergative with respect to the relativisation strategies it uses: on the one hand, the form with the suffix /-ho/, which relativises the subject-agent, or subject of transitive verbs; on the other hand, the form with the suffix /-dowa/, which relativises the patient, the subject, so to speak, of the intransitive verb and the object of the transitive verb. That is, the language treats the subject of the intransitive verb and the object of the transitive verb in the same way also with respect to the mechanisms it uses to carry out complex operations such as relativisation." (our translation of the Spanish original)

Alignment is conditioned by the semantic role of the relativised argument (agent vs. non-agent) in the relative clause, which is manifested in the choice of participial morpheme (-ho for A, -dowa for S/P).
